title: Extension by zero preserves integral constructibility and localizing categories
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion.

1. $j_!$ is exact, preserves all direct sums, preserves all limits, and
   commutes with reduction modulo $\pi_E^n$.
2. $j_!$ maps $\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$ into $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
3. $j_!$ maps $\Loc(\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E))$ into $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text: (1) Throughout, use the standing separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], $X$ and $U$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; in particular the explicit scheme hypothesis of [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits] holds. Work with the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring $A_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and its restrictions. Clause (1) of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies $j^{-1}A_X=A_U$. Give $X\setminus U$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (2). The quasi-compactness assumed for $j$ is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], which gives exactness and the module adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$. The two module categories in play are identified explicitly, not silently. For the essentially small pro-étale sites, [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] gives exact sheafification and the tensor stability of its local equivalences, so [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] applies to the commutative ring objects $A_X$ and $A_U$. It identifies the module objects $\Mod_{A_X}$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with sheaves of $A_X$-modules, and likewise on $U$. The forward functor leaves underlying abelian sheaves, sections and restriction maps unchanged. By the last paragraph of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], the module pullback $j^*$ corresponds under these equivalences to the sheaf-of-modules inverse image $j^{-1}$. Hence the left adjoints correspond too: the module extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] with $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ is, up to unique isomorphism, the ringed-site functor $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ above. Both have underlying sheaf the abelian extension by zero, and exact equivalences induce equivalences of the derived categories. Every statement below about the ringed functor therefore holds for the item's $j_!$ on $D(\Mod_{A_U})\to D(\Mod_{A_X})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], it acts termwise on the unbounded derived categories and is triangulated. Its sheaf functor preserves small sums by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] (1) both derived sums are termwise, so the derived functor preserves them too. For limits, [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits] (2), with $B=A_X$, gives preservation of products and sequential derived inverse limits. To obtain every existing small categorical limit, express it as the kernel $k:L\to P$ of $d:P\to Q$, where $P=\prod_a K_a$, $Q=\prod_{(\alpha:a\to b)}K_b$, and $d_\alpha=K(\alpha)\operatorname{pr}_a-\operatorname{pr}_b$. Complete $k$ to a triangle $L\xrightarrow{k}P\xrightarrow{q}C\xrightarrow{h}L[1]$. Consecutive maps of a distinguished triangle compose to zero: for $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\to X[1]$, (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] applied to $(1_X,u)$ from $X\xrightarrow{1}X\to0\to X[1]$ gives $c:0\to Z$ with $vu=c\circ0=0$, and (TR2) gives the other composites. The Hom sequences of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] are exact. Since $k$ is monic and $kh[-1]=0$, $h=0$. By [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split], $P$ identifies with $L\oplus C$, $k$ with the first inclusion and $q$ with the second projection. Thus $k$ has a retraction $r$ and $q$ a section $s$, with $rk=1$, $qs=1$, $qk=0$ and $1_P=kr+sq$. Put $v=ds:C\to Q$. Because $dk=0$, $d=vq$. If $vt=0$, then $dst=0$, so the kernel property factors $st$ through $k$; applying $q$ gives $t=0$. Thus $v$ is monic. Complete $v$ to a triangle $C\xrightarrow{v}Q\to D\xrightarrow{w}C[1]$. The equality $vw[-1]=0$ and monicity of $v$ give $w=0$. Applying [lem-pc-derived-zero-third-split] gives a left inverse $u:Q\to C$ of $v$. For the additive functor $F=j_!$, the identities $F(u)F(v)=1$ and $F(q)F(s)=1$ persist. If $a:T\to F(P)$ satisfies $F(d)a=0$, multiply $F(d)=F(v)F(q)$ by $F(u)$ to obtain $F(q)a=0$; then $a=F(k)F(r)a$ by $1=F(k)F(r)+F(s)F(q)$. The factor is unique because $F(r)F(k)=1$, proving that $F(k)$ is the kernel of $F(d)$. Product preservation therefore carries the displayed limit cone to a limit cone. Here 'preserves all limits' means all small categorical limits that exist; it does not assert that an arbitrary triangulated category is complete. The same clause holds for module sheaves, the level of Stacks Tag 09BP. Clause (3) of [det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits] gives preservation of products of module sheaves. Exactness gives preservation of kernels. Every small limit is the kernel of the displayed difference map $d$ between two products, so $j_!$ preserves all small limits of module sheaves. For the optional exponent $n=0$, reduction is tensoring with the zero coefficient ring, so both reduced complexes are zero and commute with the additive functor. For $n\geq1$, [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] identifies reduction modulo $\pi_E^n$ with the cone of scalar multiplication by $\pi_E^n$. The module-linear exact termwise functor preserves this cone: its terms, finite direct sums, differentials and scalar multiplication agree with the cone on $j_!K$. The comparison is natural in $K$; on the rank-one resolutions the transition from $n+1$ to $n$ is multiplication by $\pi_E$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$, which $j_!$ preserves, so the reductions and their transitions commute with $j_!$.

(2) We read the item in the standing separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting fixed by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], as in the cited integral lemmas. The integral tensor lemma [sk-lem-int-tensor] states that extension by zero along a quasi-compact open immersion and direct image along a closed immersion preserve $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$. Hence $j_!K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ for every $K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$.

(3) Use [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] (2) with the arbitrary generating class $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ for $T=U,X$; it defines the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory closed under small sums for precisely this class. In the ambient category $D(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, let $\mathcal S$ be the full subcategory of all $K$ for which $j_!K\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$. It is replete; exactness in (1) makes it closed under shifts and distinguished triangles, and preservation of sums in (1) makes it closed under arbitrary small sums. Hence it is localizing. By (2) it contains $\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$, so minimality gives $\Loc(\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E))\subseteq\mathcal S$, proving the required inclusion. This applies the arbitrary-class localizing closure directly, without using a definition restricted to $\Dctf$.
